title: SEM Imaging of Battery Materials by Secondary Electron Energy Filtering
content: Identifying carbon allotropes such as graphite and amorphous carbon, as well as organic materials like polymers, using compositional contrast from backscattered electron signal is challenging. We have investigated the differentiation of carbon materials and polymer materials using ultra-low voltage scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observation [1], but the identification of carbon allotropes remains difficult. In this study, we attempted to distinguish materials based on differences in their secondary electron (SE) energy spectra. Using the SE-bandpass energy filtering (BPF) method [2], we compared and verified the energy spectra obtained from polymers, graphite, and amorphous carbon contained in the anode active materials of lithium-ion batteries (LiB).
